value: maximum Doppler shift compensation magnitude 83.9%, ranging from 72.3 to 92.6% across individual bats
method: behavioural: moving-pendulum paradigm; the bat was body-restrained in a holder on the pendulum with the head free, released from about 45 degrees and swung toward a reflective board, calls recorded by a microphone 7 cm in front of the nose; compensation magnitude = percentage of the bat's maximum call-frequency reduction during the swing relative to the Doppler-induced change in resting frequency expected from the pendulum speed (resting frequency taken before swing onset), computed per trial
conditions: Laboratory test room; four adult male wild-caught bats in the pendulum test (hand nets, daytime, a cave near Xianning City, Hubei, China; housed in groups of two to five at about 24 C on a reversed 12:12 light cycle), 18 to 20 trials per bat, 75 in all; bat-to-board distance 0.2 to 2.56 m (the Methods elsewhere place a wooden board 1.5 m in front of the pendulum; the text is inconsistent); pendulum reached 3.34 +/- 0.09 m/s with a 2.56 +/- 0.03 s period; 83.9% is the median over pendulum trials (free-flight median 87.2%); in echo playback (frequency shifts of 0, 700 and -700 Hz) bats showed no consistent audiovocal adjustments, so the compensation was not reproduced with playback; data collection began after about 2 months of training; the paper states neither time in captivity nor any anaesthesia or drug use; precision (0.27%) is a separate measure not claimed here; the paper does not say whether 72.3 to 92.6% are per-bat medians; Abstract rounds the pendulum value to 84%

Resting frequency not found in a quotable sentence, so not filed.

value: ossicular chain resonant frequencies 71 to 200 Hz, not significantly different between vertical and lateral stimulation
method: biophysical: scanning laser Doppler vibrometry of ossicular velocity in dissected skulls under a periodic seismic chirp (10 to 600 Hz, 1 s, 1 Hz resolution), velocities averaged five times per point
conditions: Laboratory, euthanised animals (isoflurane overdose) with dissected skulls, so a mechanical response of the middle ear and not a neural or behavioural threshold; seven adult Cape golden moles in the study (four females, three males), five used for the seismic experiments and two as controls (per the paper's Methods as read through a summary tool); resonant frequencies mean 135.7 +/- 49 Hz (s.d.) in the Results; stimulation tested from 10 to 600 Hz in two directions (vertical, lateral); the 71 to 200 Hz range is across 10 ears of the five measured animals; resonance = first resonance of the malleus motion relative to the skull, skull halved frontally and its dorsal part mounted on a shaker-driven aluminium block; the authors state that sensing substrate vibration by inertial bone conduction 'has never been conclusively demonstrated'

source.authors: Willi UB, Bronner GN, Narins PM
source.title: Middle ear dynamics in response to seismic stimuli in the Cape golden mole (Chrysochloris asiatica)

quote: Resonant frequencies were found between 71 and 200 Hz and did not differ significantly between the two stimulation directions.
note: Free-to-read PDF on the publisher's host (silverchair, Company of Biologists); it prints only a copyright line and no Creative Commons licence. The PDF typesets '200 Hz' with a thin dot (200·Hz); an ordinary space is used here. Read through a page summary tool, which gave the full abstract sentence after the first reply cut it at '200'. Specimen counts and euthanasia come from that tool's reading of the Methods; no behavioural or neural data on seismic hearing in this species in this paper. Mammal Diversity Database lists Chrysochloris asiatica as valid (Chrysochloridae, Afrosoricida). Crossref: issued 2006-01-15, volume 209 issue 2, pages 302-313.

value: lowest threshold of all size groups from 50 Hz to 2 kHz was 81.6 dB re 1 µPa at 1 kHz, in the largest size group (XL)
method: auditory evoked potential (AEP) audiometry with tone bursts (Blackman-gated); threshold = lowest sound pressure level giving a repeatable AEP trace by overlaying replicate traces
conditions: Laboratory; aquarium-bred fish from a Vienna breeder, in five size groups (XS to XL); group XL is SL 68.9 to 83.9 mm, 8.43 to 15.8 g, N = 7 (Methods list other group sizes N = 8, 10, 7, 8, 7 whereas the Figure 4 caption gives 7, 7, 7, 8, 7); thresholds measured at 0.05, 0.07, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 kHz, so the 1 kHz minimum lies inside the tested range; fish in S to XL were mildly immobilised with Flaxedil (gallamine triethiodide), the XS group (SL 11.3 to 15.3 mm) was not; water kept at 25 +/- 1 C; fish in a plastic tub 33 cm across and 13 cm deep with 1 cm gravel, lined with air-filled packing wrap against reflections, loudspeakers in air 0.5 m above the water, hydrophone about 1 cm from the head (thresholds are tub SPL values, not free-field); Flaxedil dose 0.3 to 1.81 mg/g; 1000 stimuli at each polarity averaged into a 2000-stimulus trace; sound pressure level only, particle motion not stated as measured; smaller fish were less sensitive, XS fish did not respond above 3 kHz (only two of six at 3 kHz)
